body.statement: For every \(A\subseteq V\), the state \(C_A\) equals covariance after orthogonal projection on the span of the coordinates indexed by \(A\) and is independent of the order in which \(A\) was removed. A permutation \(\pi\) belongs to \(\Pi_S(\mathcal O_S)\) if and only if \(\pi(k)\) is removable at \(A_{k-1}=\{\pi(1),\ldots,\pi(k-1)\}\) for every \(k\). Thus source-to-sink paths in \(\mathcal D_S\) are in bijection with compatible orders, and all states and removable edges can be constructed in \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p)\) exact-real arithmetic operations and \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p)\) memory.
body.justification: Path independence is the step that replaces factorial order search by a memoized subset-state representation.
body.gap: Section 3.1 of DirectLiNGAM identifies one exogenous variable in Lemma 1, closes the non-Gaussian LiNGAM model after removing that true root in Lemma 2, and preserves the remaining causal order in Corollary 1. The recursive proof supporting Section 4.6 of HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM likewise follows roots licensed by its diversity score. Neither source proves that all sequential projections reaching the same removed set have an identical covariance state, nor gives necessary-and-sufficient steps whose complete source-to-sink paths are exactly all compatible orders. GhoshalHonorio2018LinearSEM uses a Schur update in a different point-identified sink model.
body.consumer: The subset DAG supplies a complete feasibility oracle and the finite state space required by quotient enumeration and calibration design.
